title: Finite support of higher direct images
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-morphism-conventions, def-pc-scheme]. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ [pqf-def-coherent], (1) each $R^if_*\mathcal{F}$ is quasi-coherent. If $S$ is quasi-compact, there is an integer $n=n(X,S,f)$ such that (2) $R^pf_*\mathcal{F}=0$ for every $p\ge n$ and every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{F}$, and (3) for every morphism $g:S'\to S$ of schemes, with $X'=S'\times_S X$ [def-pc-fibre-product], projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$, and every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-module $\mathcal{F}'$, one has $R^p f'_*\mathcal{F}'=0$ for every $p\ge n$.

proof.text: Choose affine neighbourhoods U_t of all points of T. Their inverse images are quasi-compact and quasi-separated because f is qcqs. Apply the uniform affine-pullback cohomology bound to each inverse-image scheme, independently of the coefficient module.

Compactness of T selects finitely many U_t. Take N to be the maximum of their bounds (Finset.sup, including empty T). For any cartesian base change, cover T-prime by all affine opens V lying in the inverse image of one selected U_t. The restricted cartesian square gives an affine morphism f-prime^{-1}V -> f^{-1}U_t: it is the base change of V -> U_t, a morphism between affine schemes. The chosen bound therefore makes H^p(f-prime^{-1}V,F-prime) subsingleton for p>=N.

The open-module-cohomology comparison identifies the vanishing group with the right-derived sections over f-prime^{-1}V. The affine-open higher-direct-image sections isomorphism identifies it with sections of R^p f-prime_* F-prime over V. Quasi-coherence and surjectivity of the zero endomorphism on this affine cover imply it is epi; cancelling it shows id=0, hence the sheaf is zero.
